question: In the United States, for Q4 2019 and Q4 2020, first select only those cities where total sales (with no promotions) rose by at least 20% from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020. Among these cities, rank products by their overall sales (still excluding promotions) in those quarters and take the top 20%. Then compute each top product’s share of total sales in Q4 2019 and Q4 2020 and calculate the difference in share from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020, returning the results in descending order of that share change.
sql:
WITH city_sales AS (
    SELECT s.prod_id, c.cust_city, s.amount_sold, t.calendar_quarter_id
    FROM sales s
    JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
    JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    WHERE co.country_name = 'United States of America'
      AND s.promo_id = 999
      AND t.calendar_quarter_id IN (1772, 1776)
),
city_q_sales AS (
    SELECT cust_city, calendar_quarter_id, SUM(amount_sold) as total_sales
    FROM city_sales
    GROUP BY cust_city, calendar_quarter_id
),
city_growth AS (
    SELECT q2020.cust_city
    FROM city_q_sales q2020
    JOIN city_q_sales q2019 ON q2020.cust_city = q2019.cust_city
    WHERE q2020.calendar_quarter_id = 1776
      AND q2019.calendar_quarter_id = 1772
      AND 1.0 * (q2020.total_sales - q2019.total_sales) / q2019.total_sales >= 0.20
),
product_sales AS (
    SELECT cs.prod_id, cs.calendar_quarter_id, SUM(cs.amount_sold) as prod_sales
    FROM city_sales cs
    JOIN city_growth cg ON cs.cust_city = cg.cust_city
    GROUP BY cs.prod_id, cs.calendar_quarter_id
),
product_totals AS (
    SELECT prod_id, SUM(prod_sales) as total_prod_sales
    FROM product_sales
    GROUP BY prod_id
),
ranked_products AS (
    SELECT pt.prod_id, pt.total_prod_sales,
           NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY pt.total_prod_sales DESC) as tile
    FROM product_totals pt
)
SELECT tile, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM ranked_products GROUP BY tile ORDER BY tile
